correctness.rationale: The directed length-n overlap graph of words avoiding 000 and 111 has 2F_(n+1) edges. Degree imbalance +1 occurs at 2F_(n−3) vertices with doubled first pair and undoubled last pair, obliging at least that many deletions for a closed trail with distinct windows. Deleting precisely the edges doubled at BOTH ends cancels all imbalances. Alternating extensions prove the retained graph is strongly connected, so it has an Euler tour of length 2(F_(n+1)−F_(n−3)). At equality an alternative deleted outgoing edge would terminate at a zero-imbalance vertex without outgoing deletion, so all deletions are forced, proving canonical window-set rigidity. Independent graph enumeration, Euler cycle and actual cyclic windows checked n=4..13. Infinite proof uses graph balance, not extrapolation.
residual_risks: Finite direct Euler verification checks only n<=13; correct connectivity and forced balance arguments must carry all larger n.
